historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Anthraquinone stimulant laxatives

starting.description: The purgative effect of senna leaves and fruits was recognized in medicinal use, and preparations were developed from the plant; the first observer and initial circumstances are not established.

inspiration.description: Observed purgative activity of senna plant material in medicinal use; the original individual observation is not described.

steps.description: A modern historical account connects recognition of senna's purgative action with the use of its powders and preparations. By 1949 senna leaf and pod were established vegetable purgatives.

Fairbairn reports earlier crystallization of sennosides A and B and investigates active constituents of already used plant purgatives; the 1949 Stoll and colleagues abstract describes their isolation and purification method.

Later researchers compare variable liquid senna preparations with a dry granular senna-pod preparation using chemical, animal, and clinical assessments; they report stability and activity for the tested dry preparation.

design.description: Researchers isolated and crystallized natural senna glycosides, compared their biological activity with chemically treated fractions, developed chemical and biological assays, and evaluated a dry granular preparation to address consistency and stability of the established plant drug. The sources do not establish a newly designed active molecule or identify who invented the granular formulation.

circumstances.description: Fairbairn's comparison of purified and chemically altered sennoside A was a planned experiment; the circumstances of the original observation remain unknown.

limits: The frozen class packet has only senna; other plants are contextual, not separate cohort medicines. The classification is not an independently traced founding history for every anthracene-containing plant.
Sennosides A and B are important active senna constituents, but their exclusive responsibility for crude senna activity is not established; E10 records a historical challenge to that inference.
conflicts: E10: Fairbairn and Saleh's 1951 preview questions whether the whole activity of crude senna can be attributed to sennosides A and B alone. It does not contradict the accounts that these are major constituents or identify a different founding origin; the remainder of their report was not read.
gaps: The initial observer, circumstances and precise date of the original observation are not established; the ninth-century claim is a later historical account whose underlying early sources were not read.
Stoll and colleagues' 1941 proceedings report and the body of their 1949 isolation article were not read; only the 1949 abstract and references were accessible.
The middle pages of the 1957 clinical report and its earlier formulation source were not read; formulation inventor and design details are not established.
The 1951 Fairbairn and Saleh letter was accessible only as a short opening preview; its results and the claimed synergy were not read.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Longstanding senna laxative use and variable preparations supported constituent and formulation work.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: The first human observer and a unique initiating episode are not established.
